Dear Principal Marsh,

I heard about the new rule you are thinking about, where you have to have a B average to be in sports or other activities. I want to tell you why I think that would be a bad idea, and I hope you will listen because a lot of students feel the same way I do.

First of all, a lot of us only come to school because of our activities. That sounds bad to say but it is true. My friend Devon is on the wrestling team and he says practice is the only part of the day he actually looks forward to. If you take that away from him because he got a C in science, then what does he have left? He is not going to suddenly start studying harder. He is just going to stop caring about school at all. I think you would end up with more kids skipping and less kids trying, which is the opposite of what you want.

Second, a C average is not failing. A C means you passed. It means you did the work and you understood enough to move on. If a C is good enough to get you to the next grade, I don't see why it is not good enough to let you run track. It feels like you are punishing people for being average, and most people are average, that is kind of what average means.

Also, sports actually help your grades. When I was in cross country last fall I had to get my homework done before practice or my mom would not let me go. I had a schedule. Now that the season is over I stay up late and do my homework at 11 at night and my grades went down, not up. Coach Reyes checked our grades every week and if you were slipping he made you sit with him and do work before you could run. That helped way more than just kicking someone off the team would have.

I do think grades matter and I am not saying people should be allowed to fail everything and still play. Maybe a rule where you can't be failing two or more classes would make sense, or a rule where if your grades drop you have to go to tutoring on Tuesdays but you can still play. That way the school is helping instead of just taking something away.

Please think about the kids who are trying their best and still only getting a C. They deserve to be part of things too.

Sincerely,
A student in 8th grade

Dear Principal Davis,

I heard that you are thinking about making a rule that students need at least a B average to be in sports or other activities. I understand why you would want that, because school work should come first. But I think this rule would end up hurting the students it is supposed to help, and I am asking you not to do it.

The first reason is that for a lot of kids, the activity is the only thing keeping them coming to school. My cousin Tyler was almost failing two classes last year until he made the wrestling team. Coach Meyer told him he had to show his grades every Friday, and Tyler actually started doing his homework because he did not want to sit out a match. He is not a B student. He is a C student who tries hard. Under the new rule he never would have been allowed on the team in the first place, and nobody would have been checking his grades at all. He would have just gone home after school and played video games, and his grades would be worse, not better.

The second reason is that a C average does not always mean a student is being lazy. Some people are just not good test takers. Some people have to watch their little brothers and sisters until their mom gets home at seven, or they have a job, or English is not their first language. A student like that might be working twice as hard as somebody with an A and still have a C on the report card. Punishing them by taking away the one hour a day they actually enjoy does not seem fair, and it would not teach them anything except that school does not care why they are struggling.

Third, activities teach things classes do not. In band I learned that if I do not practice, twenty other people sound bad because of me. On the track team you learn that you get out what you put in. Those lessons are worth just as much as a quiz grade, and the students with C averages are probably the ones who need them most.

I also think the teams and clubs themselves would fall apart. A lot of our players have C averages. If half the soccer team is cut in October, we would not even be able to field a team, and the kids with the B averages would lose their season too for no reason.

Instead of banning people, I think you could make a rule that anybody below a certain grade has to go to tutoring twice a week or to a study hall before practice. Then students would still get help, coaches could still keep track of them, and nobody would lose the thing that makes them want to be here. That would fix the actual problem, which is grades, without taking away the thing that is working.

Thank you for asking what students think about this. I hope you will consider keeping activities open to everybody who is willing to work for them.

Sincerely,
Jordan Alvarez
8th Grade

I am writing to tell you that I think this rule is a bad idea, and I have three reasons.

My first reason is that for some kids, sports are the only thing keeping them in school at all. My friend Marcus is in seventh period study hall with me and he is not great at math, he has like a C in it, but he is one of the best players on the basketball team. When he got benched for two games last year for being late a bunch of times, he stopped doing his homework completely. He said what's the point. The rule is supposed to make people study more but I think for a lot of kids it would do the exact opposite, because the thing they cared about would be gone.

My second reason is that a C average does not always mean a student is being lazy. Some people have really hard classes. If you take advanced science and algebra you might get a C in those, but somebody else taking easier classes could get all B's without trying very hard. That doesn't seem fair, because the person working harder is the one who gets punished. Also some kids have stuff going on at home that nobody at school knows about. My cousin had a rough year when her parents split up and her grades dropped to C's and D's and volleyball was honestly the only normal part of her week. Taking that away from someone during their worst year would just make everything worse for them.

My third reason is that activities actually teach you things you cannot learn in a classroom. In band I learned how to practice something over and over even when I was bad at it, which is basically what studying is. On teams you learn to show up on time, work with people you don't like, and keep going when you're losing. Those are real skills. If we only let the B students have them, then the students who probably need to learn responsibility the most are the ones who never get the chance.

I understand why you might want this rule. Grades are important and school should come first, I agree with that part. Nobody should be failing every class and still playing every game. But I think there is a better way to do it. Instead of a B average, you could make it so anybody failing a class has to go to tutoring twice a week to stay eligible. That way the kid actually gets help with the subject they are struggling in, instead of just losing the one thing they were good at. Our coaches already check grades every few weeks, so it would not even be that hard to set up.

Please think about this before you decide. A lot of good students with C averages would be sitting at home instead of being here after school where teachers can keep an eye on them. I think the rule would hurt the exact people it is trying to help.

Thank you for reading my letter and for listening to what students think.

Sincerely,
A concerned 8th grade student

Dear Principal Reyes,

I heard about the new rule you are thinking about, where you have to have a B average to be in sports or clubs. I know you want people to take their classes more seriously and I get that, but I think this rule would actually hurt the students it is supposed to help. I am writing to ask you not to do it.

The first reason is that a lot of kids only come to school because of their activity. My cousin was failing almost everything in seventh grade until he joined wrestling. His coach checks his grades every Friday and if he is missing work he has to sit out practice and do it in the library. That made him go from D's to mostly C's and one B. If your rule had existed he never would have been allowed on the team in the first place, so nobody would have been checking his work at all, and he would probably still be failing. Taking away the thing that makes someone show up is not going to make them study more. It just makes them not show up.

The second reason is that not everybody's C means the same thing. Some people get C's because they goof off. But some people get C's because they take care of their little brothers and sisters after school, or because they are still learning English, or because they have a learning disability and a C is honestly them trying as hard as they can. My friend Dalia has an IEP and she works harder than anyone I know and she still has like a 2.4. Is it fair that she loses band, which is the one class she is actually great at, when somebody else who barely tries gets to stay in because school is just easy for them? That is punishing people for what they struggle with instead of for how much effort they put in.

The third reason is that a lot of us need these activities for later. If you want to get into a good high school program or someday get a scholarship, they do not just look at grades, they look at what you did. Students with a C average are exactly the ones who need something extra on there. Cutting them out means the kids who are already doing fine keep getting ahead and everybody else falls further behind.

I do think there should be some kind of rule, just not this one. I think it would be way better to say you cannot be failing a class, which is what my old school did. Or you could do a study hall requirement where if your grade drops below a C you have to go to tutoring twice a week to stay on the team. That way the grades still matter but you do not lose the students completely.

Thank you for asking us what we think. Not every principal does that and we appreciate it.

Sincerely,
Marcus Dunn
8th Grade

Dear Principal,

I heard about the new rule you are thinking about, where you have to have a B average to be in sports or any other activity. I know you are probably trying to help us do better in school, and I get why you would think that. But I think this rule would end up hurting the students it is supposed to help, and I want to explain why.

The first reason is that a C is still passing. If a student has a C average it means they are doing the work and they are getting by, maybe not great, but they are not failing anything. Punishing somebody for a grade that the school itself says is okay does not really seem fair. If a C is bad enough to get you kicked off the team, then why is it a passing grade at all?

My second reason, and I think this is the big one, is that sports and clubs are the reason some kids even show up. My cousin was in seventh grade last year and he hated almost every part of school except wrestling. His grades were not amazing, like a C average or maybe a little under, but he came every single day because he knew if he missed school he could not practice. If you had taken wrestling away from him, he would not have suddenly started studying more. He would have just stopped caring. That is what I think would really happen with this policy. You would take away the one thing holding a bunch of C students to this school and expect them to work harder, and instead a lot of them would work less.

Also, being in an activity actually helps your grades in ways people do not always notice. When I have practice after school I have to get my homework done in a certain window, so I do it. During the off season I put everything off until 10:00 at night. Coaches check on us, they ask about our tests, and my coach makes anybody with a missing assignment sit out the first ten minutes of practice. That is more people checking on my grades than I would have otherwise. Clubs and teams are not competing with school work, they are part of what keeps some of us organized.

I also think you should remember that not everybody has the same situation at home. Some kids have to watch their younger brothers and sisters, some do not have a quiet place to study or somebody who can help them with math. Those students are the most likely to have a C average and they are also the ones who need a team or a club the most, because it gives them somewhere to go and adults who know them. A B average rule would basically take activities away from the students with the hardest lives and leave them for the students who already have everything going for them.

I am not saying grades should not matter at all. I just think there are better ways to do this. You could require a weekly grade check, so anybody who is failing a class has to go to tutoring or study hall before they can play that week. That way the student gets actual help with the class they are struggling in instead of just losing their sport. You could also do a probation system, where if your grades drop you have a few weeks to bring them up while you are still on the team. That keeps the pressure on but it does not throw people away.

Thank you for asking us what we think about this. I hope you will consider keeping the requirement at passing grades and adding more support instead, because I really believe that would raise more grades than a B average rule ever would.

Sincerely,
An eighth grade student

We would probably have to cancel some of them because we wouldn't have enough players. The band might not have enough people for a full song. That's not making our school better, that's just making it emptier.

Another thing is that grades don't always show how hard someone is trying. Some kids have jobs after school or watch their little brothers and sisters while their parents work. Some kids have learning problems and work really hard for a C, way harder than a kid who gets a B without studying. It doesn't seem fair that the kid who tried the hardest gets punished and the one who barely tried gets to play. If we're going to have a rule, it should be about effort, like you have to be passing everything and not be missing assignments, not a number that doesn't tell the whole story.

In drama club I learned to talk in front of people without shaking. Those things help me in my classes too. Being on a team taught me to manage my time because I knew I only had from 6 to 8 to do homework, so I actually did it instead of putting it off all night. That way students get help instead of just getting cut. That actually fixes the problem, and it doesn't punish people for being average.

Thank you for asking us what we think. Not every principal does that, and I really appreciate it. I hope you'll think about what I said.

Sincerely,
A 8th grade student

essays.text:
Dear Principal,

I heard that you are thinking about making a new rule where a student has to have a B average or they can't play sports or be in clubs. I know a lot of kids are writing you about this so I will try to be quick, but I really hope you read mine because I think this rule would hurt the exact people it is supposed to help.

My first reason is that for a lot of students, sports or band or whatever they are in is the only reason they come to school in a good mood. My friend Tyler has a C in math and a C in science and he is on the wrestling team. He never misses practice, not one time, even when it snowed. Last year he got hurt and couldn't wrestle for about six weeks, and everybody thought his grades would go up because he had more time. They went down instead. He told me it was because when he had practice he knew he had to finish his work before 3:30 or Coach would bench him, and when he wasn't wrestling there was no reason to finish anything. If you take the sport away from a kid like that, you are not giving him more study time. You are taking away the one thing that was making him study at all.

My second reason is that a C is not a bad grade. A C means average. It means you showed up, you did the work, and you understood most of it. I feel like this rule treats a C like it is a punishment somebody earned when really a lot of C students are trying as hard as the A students. My cousin is in eighth grade too and she has a C average, and she also watches her little brother every day until her mom gets home at 7. She is not lazy, she just has less time than other people have. A rule like this would punish her for her mom's work schedule, which is not fair.

Also I want to say that we already have a rule about this. Right now if you are failing a class you can't play until you bring it up, and that rule makes sense to me because failing means you are actually not learning the material. Moving the line all the way up to a B is a huge jump. I did the math on the roster of my sister's volleyball team and she said about half of them are C students, so you might not even have enough players for a team, and then the A students who worked hard don't get a season either.

I know somebody is going to say that school is for learning and sports come second, and I agree with that. I'm not saying grades don't matter. What I would say instead is keep the no-failing rule, and if somebody's grade drops to a C or lower, make them go to a study hall twice a week with a teacher before practice. That way they get the help and they still get the team. Taking someone off the team doesn't teach them the material. It just makes them sit at home.

Thank you for asking us what we think about it. Not every principal would do that.

Sincerely,
A student in 8th grade
